title: Five-phase repository-local AI SDLC framework

acceptance_criteria.outcome: Natural-language intents select Discover, Plan, Build, Validate or Deploy while preserving explicit scope and authorization.
Repository-local requirement, implementation, test, finding, evidence and release artifacts have schemas, stable IDs and archive conventions.
Evidence gates reject missing, failed, skipped, stale, uncovered and invalid-waiver cases; changed plans invalidate high-risk authorization.
Risk routing covers money, OAuth/MCP, model files, nested Dockerfiles, API clients, mobile feature screens and framework policy without tiny-diff bypasses.
Verification profiles expose scope/prerequisites and framework checks run in CI; existing PG/axe coverage is retained.
Release tooling and both Cloud Build pipelines check exact-candidate unit/QA/framework CI before deployment; readiness and actual authorization remain separate.
Deploy documents both-component monitoring, observed serving versions, read-only smoke/error validation, recovery boundaries and external setup prerequisites.
Agent adapters remain thin; existing current product/QA documents stay separate from historical artifacts; no commit, push or deployment occurs during this implementation.

implementation_approval.reference: This conversation: approved detailed scope, five phases and repo storage; final instruction "start the implementation. Dont commit any code." Bootstrap record captures that prior authorization.

notes: User approved the scope and detailed five-phase design, then explicitly requested implementation without commits. Live GCP setup and installed external-agent runtime checks remain rollout prerequisites, not claimed here.
